CLAUSE 3 IS MET AND DRIVEN — verified against merged main rather than taken from the PR's claim, because it was the one clause I doubted. The clause is an ISOLATION claim ('revoking one gateway's device session breaks ONLY that entry'), which is a statement about N entries and therefore cannot be satisfied by per-outcome handling alone. desktop/connectMode.js:745 probeAll() builds a per-row health map with Promise.all over registry.endpoints and NEVER MUTATES the registry, so one row's outcome has no path to another's. THE TEST'S CONSTRUCTION IS THE LOAD-BEARING PART (desktop/test/connectMode.test.js:857): it stands up TWO REAL LISTENERS — one answering 403, one a real gatewayHandler('2.0.0') — with the stated reason that 'a single stubbed prober cannot be independent of itself'. That is right, and a shared fake would have made the whole assertion vacuous. It asserts the revoked row goes needs_pairing while the other is REACHABLE at the correct version; that the healthy row's registry entry, confirmation record and namespaced state (last.route) are untouched AND that it is still switchable — 'one endpoint's 403 is not a reason to re-pair the other'; and, separately, that a row with NO URL reports UNKNOWN rather than unreachable, which is the absent-vs-declared-false distinction again at row level. MY STATED WORRY WAS WRONG IN ITS SPECIFIC FORM AND IS RECORDED AS SUCH: I expected revocation to ride the tamper path that deliberately distrusts EVERY row on a permission change, which would have made clause 3 violated BY DESIGN. It does not — the tamper path and the per-row probe are separate seams, and the test proves the separation rather than asserting it. REUSABLE FINDING BEYOND THIS ATOM: `new URL('http://2130706433').hostname` ALREADY returns '127.0.0.1', so a loopback-spoofing refusal MUST fire on the RAW AUTHORITY TEXT — checking url.hostname cannot see the spelling it is meant to catch. Also accepted: the narrowing to refuse public plaintext, and the deliberate decision NOT to ship a MAC. FALSIFIED RATHER THAN ARGUED, which is why I accept it: the builder PLANTED the blast-radius design I was worried about — probeAll marking every row needs_pairing if any row is — grepped the mutation back on disk to confirm it was live, and it reddened exactly `marks the revoked row needs_pairing and leaves the other reachable`, then restored from a file copy with 65/65 green. Nine falsifications in all, each reddening the leg that names it. And the store-level distrust I feared it would share keys on `store.permissions.safe` — a FILESYSTEM MODE, which no HTTP status can influence. ALSO NARROWER THAN THE PLAN'S WORDING, DELIBERATELY: the plan said 'LAN or remote', but public plaintext is REFUSED rather than warned about, because a `Secure` cookie is not sent over plaintext at all — so it is broken as well as unsafe. Every non-loopback host needs one explicit confirmation recording the origin AND a resolved-address fingerprint, re-checked before each connect; hostnames are classified by what they RESOLVE to and floored at `private`, so a DNS record pointing at 127.0.0.1 never earns loopback. The capability bridge (microphone, global chord, notifications, login item) attaches ONLY to a loopback origin, with a will-navigate/will-redirect guard pinning the view to the confirmed origin — without it a link in rendered content could walk the bridge to an arbitrary origin. 351 cases / 74 suites under desktop/, up from 189. SECOND REUSABLE FINDING: Node's global agent has keepAlive:true since v19, so the builder's first liveness probe was answered from the POOLED SOCKET of a previous one and reported ECONNRESET off a stale connection. A liveness probe answerable by a connection opened before the outage is not a liveness probe. Fixed with agent:false and falsified by removing it. REMAINING: V4 only. Needs a second machine and a real tunnel; nothing local can stand in for it. The exact operator sequence is posted on #2584 and documented in docs/guides/desktop.md. |

Session 4 T4.1, T4.4 + V4; desktop/main.js + a connect dialog, coordinated with DESKTOP-CAPABILITIES; spawn-local stays the default and unchanged
